questions.title: Pop Order of a Stack
questions.description:
The LIFO principle says the element pushed LAST is popped FIRST. A stack drain therefore emits its items in reverse insertion order.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    vector<int> pop_order(const vector<int> &items)

It must return the items in the order pops would emit them (i.e. reversed).

Input Format:
Line 1: n — the number of items.
Line 2: n integers.

Output Format:
One line with the pop order, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= items[i] <= 1000000

questions.title: Top of the Stack
questions.description:
On an array-backed stack the top is simply the LAST element of the underlying vector.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int stack_top(const vector<int> &st)

It must return the top element (the last item). The stack is never empty.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n integers (bottom ... top).

Output Format:
One line with the top element.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000

questions.title: Pop One Element
questions.description:
The pop operation removes the most recently pushed element.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    vector<int> stack_pop(vector<int> st)

It must remove the top element and return the resulting stack. The harness prints the remaining elements bottom to top.

Input Format:
Line 1: n (at least 2, so the stack stays non-empty).
Line 2: n integers.

Output Format:
One line with the remaining elements, space-separated.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 1000

questions.title: Push One Element
questions.description:
The push operation places a new element on top of the stack.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    vector<int> stack_push(vector<int> st, int v)

It must append v as the new top and return the stack. The harness prints the stack bottom to top.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n integers.
Line 3: v — the value to push.

Output Format:
One line with the stack after the push, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 999, -1000000 <= v <= 1000000

questions.title: Reverse a String With a Stack
questions.description:
A classic first stack application: push every character, then pop them all — the string comes out reversed.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    string reverse_string(const string &s)

It must return the characters of s in reverse order.

Input Format:
One line: the string s (single token, no spaces).

Output Format:
One line: the reversed string.

Constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 1000

questions.title: Match Simple Parentheses
questions.description:
The simplest bracket validator: a string of '(' and ')' is balanced when every opening bracket is closed in LIFO order.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    bool is_balanced_simple(const string &s)

It must return true when s is balanced, false otherwise.

Input Format:
One line: the bracket string s (single token).

Output Format:
One line: 1 if balanced, else 0.

Constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 1000, s contains only '(' and ')'

questions.title: Browser Back Button
questions.description:
A browser keeps the visited pages in a stack-like history: the last entry is the current page. Pressing back k times lands on the entry k positions earlier.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    string back_state(const vector<string> &history, int k)

It must return the page shown after pressing back k times: history[history.size() - 1 - k].

Input Format:
Line 1: n — the number of history entries.
Line 2: n page names (single tokens).
Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the resulting page name.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= k < n

questions.title: Undo the Last Moves
questions.description:
A puzzle game records every move on a stack. Undoing m moves removes the m most recent entries.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    vector<int> undo_moves(const vector<int> &moves, int m)

It must drop the last m moves and return the remaining ones in order. At least one move always remains.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n move codes.
Line 3: m (0 <= m < n).

Output Format:
One line with the remaining moves, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= m < n

questions.title: Balanced Code Snippet
questions.description:
A code editor highlights snippets whose brackets do not nest correctly. Brackets come in three kinds: (), [] and {} — and kinds must match LIFO style.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    bool is_balanced(const string &s)

It must return true when every bracket in s is closed by the matching kind, false otherwise.

Input Format:
One line: the bracket string s (single token).

Output Format:
One line: 1 if balanced, else 0.

Constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 1000, s contains only '(', ')', '[', ']', '{', '}'

questions.title: Depth of Nested Brackets
questions.description:
A static-analysis tool reports the maximum nesting depth of a bracketed expression. The input is a balanced sequence of '(' and ')'.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int max_depth(const string &s)

It must return the maximum nesting depth (a plain "()" has depth 1).

Input Format:
One line: the bracket string s (single token, guaranteed balanced).

Output Format:
One line with the depth.

Constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 1000, s contains only '(' and ')' and is balanced

questions.title: Next Greater Element
questions.description:
A pricing dashboard shows, for every item, the first strictly greater price appearing to its right (or -1 when none exists). A stack of candidates solves this in one pass.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    vector<int> next_greater(const vector<int> &a)

It must return, for each element, the first strictly greater element to its right, or -1.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n integers.

Output Format:
One line with n answers, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 5000, -1000000000 <= a[i] <= 1000000000

questions.title: Valid Push and Pop Operations
questions.description:
An auditor replays a stack-machine trace. In the encoding, a positive value means "push that value" and 0 means "pop". The trace is valid only if no pop fires while the stack is empty.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int valid_ops(const vector<int> &ops)

It must return 1 when every pop happens on a non-empty stack, else 0.

Input Format:
Line 1: m — the number of operations.
Line 2: m integers (positive = push that value, 0 = pop).

Output Format:
One line: 1 if the trace is valid, else 0.

Constraints:
1 <= m <= 2000, 0 <= ops[i] <= 1000000000

questions.title: Min Stack Log
questions.description:
A monitoring tool keeps a running-minimum stack: alongside every pushed value it remembers the minimum of the stack so far, so each "report minimum" query is instant.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    vector<long long> min_stack_log(const vector<long long> &flat)

flat holds (op, val) pairs: op 1 pushes val, op 2 pops, op 3 records the current minimum. It must return the recorded minima in order. Pops are always valid and every query fires on a non-empty stack.

Input Format:
Line 1: m — the number of operations.
Lines 2..m+1: two integers "op val" (val is 0 for ops 2 and 3).

Output Format:
One line with the recorded minima, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= m <= 2000, -1000000000 <= val <= 1000000000

questions.title: Sort a Stack With a Helper Stack
questions.description:
A warehouse robot sorts a stack of crates using ONLY stack operations and one auxiliary stack: repeatedly pop from the input stack and insert into the helper so the helper stays ascending.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    vector<int> sort_stack(vector<int> st)

It must return the elements sorted ascending, produced purely by push/pop moves (no sorting functions).

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n integers.

Output Format:
One line with the sorted elements, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= st[i] <= 1000000

questions.title: Reverse a String Using Stack Operations
questions.description:
A message encoder reverses payloads strictly through stack discipline: push every character, then pop them into the output. No reverse utilities allowed.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    string reverse_via_stack(const string &s)

It must return s reversed using push_back / pop_back moves only.

Input Format:
One line: the string s (single token).

Output Format:
One line: the reversed string.

Constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 1000

questions.title: Minimum Bracket Removals
questions.description:
A linter counts how many brackets must be deleted to make a '(' / ')' string balanced. A stack pass finds every unmatched bracket.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int min_removals(const string &s)

It must return the minimum number of brackets to remove.

Input Format:
One line: the bracket string s (single token).

Output Format:
One line with the count.

Constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 1000, s contains only '(' and ')'

questions.title: Postfix Expression Evaluation
questions.description:
A reverse-polish calculator reads tokens left to right: numbers are pushed, and each operator pops two operands, applies itself, and pushes the result back.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long eval_postfix(const vector<string> &tokens)

It must return the value of the postfix expression. Tokens are non-negative integers or one of + - * /. Division is exact integer division and every division divides evenly.

Input Format:
Line 1: n — the number of tokens.
Line 2: n tokens (single tokens, space-separated).

Output Format:
One line with the final value.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, operands are 0..1000000, expression is valid, divisions divide evenly
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 2000, operands 0..1000000, valid expression, exact divisions

questions.title: Stock Span
questions.description:
A trading terminal shows, for each day, the stock span: the number of consecutive days (including today) the price has been at most today's price. A monotonic stack answers every day in O(1) amortised time.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    vector<int> stock_span(const vector<int> &prices)

It must return the span of every day.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n prices.

Output Format:
One line with n spans, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 5000, 0 <= prices[i] <= 1000000000

questions.title: Largest Rectangle in a Histogram
questions.description:
A skyline analyser finds the largest rectangle that fits entirely inside a histogram: for every bar it extends left and right while neighbouring bars are at least as tall. A monotonic stack finds each bar's reach in one pass.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long largest_rectangle(const vector<int> &heights)

It must return the maximum rectangle area.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n bar heights.

Output Format:
One line with the largest area.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= heights[i] <= 10000

questions.title: Simplify a File Path
questions.description:
A shell normalises absolute paths with a stack of components: '.' means stay, '..' pops one level, and everything else is pushed. The canonical form starts with '/' and has no trailing slash (the root simplifies to "/").

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    string simplify_path(const string &path)

It must return the simplified path.

Input Format:
One line: the path (single token, starts with '/', components are letters, digits or dots).

Output Format:
One line with the simplified path.

Constraints:
1 <= |path| <= 1000
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= |path| <= 1000, absolute path with dot components allowed
